summary: US equities closed flat on 2026-10-13 (S&P 500 down 0.02 percent) but the tape was split: Asian memory stocks slumped, SK Hynix down 10.0935 percent and Samsung Electronics down 7.3852 percent, Micron closed 3.6247 percent lower, the memory basket fell 3.3529 percent and semiconductor equipment 2.3011 percent; meanwhile consumer electronics rose 1.8464 percent and digital advertising 0.8226 percent, with 12 of 22 themes improving on the prior session. The composite risk score is 53.05 (caution), 3.66 below the same-day 10:37Z generation at 56.71 and 1.64 below 2026-10-12 at 54.69; VIX rose from 14.84 to 15.21, the 10-year real rate at 2.91 percent sits in the 99.68 percentile, and HY OAS narrowed to 3.11 percent. The measured decline in risk came mainly from cross-asset confirmation falling from 0.75 to 0.50, a counting change rather than a broadly better tape.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation fell to 0.50 (4 of 8 production signals triggered); the 15 percent weight dimension contributes 7.5 points, the model's largest single driver; the triggered items are a lower S&P, dollar strength, real-rate pressure and small-cap underperformance.

The 10-year real rate at 2.91 percent sits at the 99.68 percentile with a risk score of 99.68 and a 4.984 point contribution; the nominal 10-year yield at 5.24 percent is at the 99.52 percentile with a 4.952 point contribution. Together they are the core pressure in the macro dimension's 73.84 score.
The high-yield spread at 3.11 percent contributes 4.6328 points and, although narrower than 3.15 percent, remains the largest single item in the 59.91 liquidity dimension.

Overnight reverse repo fell to 0.275 trillion, at the 1.77 percentile; the neutral direction rule produces a risk score of 96.47 and a 3.8588 point contribution. The reading is near zero, a mechanical high score rather than new liquidity stress.

Small-cap relative weakness reached 9.5212 (a negative value) with a risk score of 74.04, the largest pressure item in the 59.26 equity-structure dimension; breadth above the 200-day average fell to 0.5419.

supporting_signals.claim: The memory chain weakened for a second session: Micron fell 3.6247 percent and the memory basket 3.3529 percent; the two Asian giants slumped, SK Hynix down 10.0935 percent and Samsung Electronics down 7.3852 percent; A-share memory names also slipped, ChangXin Memory down 2.7927 percent.
Semiconductor equipment fell 2.3011 percent, materially weaker than the 0.1744 percent decline in the broader semiconductor group; the equipment chain is the weakest link within AI hardware.

Across assets, three risk signals fired together: the dollar index at 121.6023, the 10-year real rate at 2.91 percent and a lower S&P; the double-high combination of dollar and real rates still weighs on valuations.
VIX rose from 14.84 to 15.21 and the volatility dimension moved from 15.93 to 18.00, the largest dimension increase of the day and opposite in direction to the composite's decline.
The new-lows ratio at 0.1218 exceeds the new-highs ratio at 0.0513, and only 84 of 155 names sit above the 200-day average, so marginal breadth is weak.

contradicting_signals.claim: Credit markets did not deteriorate: HY OAS narrowed from 3.15 percent to 3.11 percent and IG OAS held at 0.83 percent, indicating the pullback is concentrated in growth and memory names rather than systemic credit stress.
The composite risk score fell 3.66 to 53.05, holding the caution level; against 2026-10-12 at 54.69 it is only 1.64 lower, so measured risk did not rise on the day.

Cross-asset confirmation at 0.50 is exactly 4 of 8 signals, a count-type reading; the dimension's 25.00 point fall (from 75.00 to 50.00) almost alone explains the 3.66 decline in the composite, so the score move reflects counting structure rather than a deterioration in prices.

The model still classifies the regime as goldilocks (low volatility, positive momentum, healthy breadth); the trend dimension at 42.49 is the lower-middle of the 6 dimensions, with price 7.4871 percent above the 200-day average.

12 of 22 sectors and themes improved versus the prior session reading: consumer electronics rose 1.8464 percent, digital advertising 0.8226 percent and fintech 0.2778 percent, so the de-rating has not spread across every growth segment.
This layer spans several data vintages: rates and the real rate come from 2026-10-09, credit spreads from 2026-10-12 and CPI from 2026-08-01, so cross-reading must respect each reference date.

6 themes (cloud computing, cybersecurity, enterprise software, semiconductors, internet platforms and gaming) are read from their ETFs (SKYY, CIBR, IGV, SOXX, FDN, ESPO); the listed constituents are illustrative only and the value is not the equal-weight basket.

what_changed_today: Composite risk score 53.05 (caution), down 3.66 from the same-day 10:37Z generation at 56.71 and only 1.64 below 2026-10-12 at 54.69.
Note that trend_1d of negative 3.66 compares against an earlier generation on the same calendar day, not against the prior trading day, which is negative 1.64.

Cross-asset confirmation fell from 0.75 to 0.50: bitcoin up 0.18155 and gold down 0.2386 in absolute terms switched two signals off while the high-yield versus Treasury relative signal switched on; the dimension moved from 75.00 to 50.00.

The AI-hardware de-rating narrowed versus 2026-10-12: memory from 4.7775 to 3.3529 percent, networking from 4.8175 to 0.1853 percent and robotics from 2.4432 to 0.6232 percent, with 12 of 22 themes improving.

The memory chain came under pressure for a second day: Micron fell 3.6247 percent; the two Korean giants slumped, SK Hynix down 10.0935 percent and Samsung Electronics down 7.3852 percent; A-share memory closed lower, ChangXin Memory down 2.7927 percent and GigaDevice down 1.4863 percent.

The A-share leg is back on the current session: ChangXin Memory at 46.99, GigaDevice at 306.22 and Longsys at 271.20 are all 2026-10-13 closes and the daily changes are single-session; the one-session regression seen after the 2026-10-12 close did not recur.

Rates: the 10-year yield at 5.24 percent and the 2-year at 4.80 percent left the 10-year minus 2-year spread narrowing from 0.47 to 0.44 (a flatter curve); the 10-year real rate rose from 2.87 to 2.91 percent, at the 99.68 percentile.

VIX rose from 14.84 to 15.21; overnight reverse repo fell to 0.275 trillion (1.77 percentile); the dollar index stands at 121.6023 and its data vintage has advanced from 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-09, aligning with the rates leg for the first time.

The policy path repriced hawkish: the FedWatch implied rate is 4.085 with the action flagged as a hike and the effective fed funds rate at 3.88 percent; Williams called one more hike this year appropriate with none needed in 2027, and Collins expects a further increase by year-end.
Bank earnings opened mixed: Goldman Sachs earned 17.01 per share against 12.86 expected, a large beat, while JPMorgan's 5.75 came in below the 5.93 expected.
watch_next: US CPI on 2026-10-14 at 12:30Z (high importance). With the real rate at 2.91 percent in the 99.68 percentile and the market already priced for a hike, this print is the largest swing factor for the composite.
TSMC reports on 2026-10-15 (expected 4.45) alongside PPI and retail sales, the demand-side read for semiconductors while memory is under pressure.

Watch whether the Korean memory slump (SK Hynix down 10.0935 percent, Samsung Electronics down 7.3852 percent) keeps transmitting into US and A-share memory; the memory basket remains the weakest sector at 3.3529 percent lower.
Bank of America reports on 2026-10-14 (expected 1.10); with HY OAS at 3.11 percent and IG OAS at 0.83 percent, use it to judge whether credit stays calm.
The 10-year minus 2-year spread is 0.44 with the 2-year at 4.80 percent; watch whether hike pricing flattens the curve further or inverts it.
Small-cap relative weakness at 9.5212 (negative) with the new-lows ratio at 0.1218 above the new-highs ratio at 0.0513; further breadth erosion would challenge the goldilocks regime call.
Earnings cluster from 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-22 for Netflix, Tesla, GM and GE, with Tesla expected at 0.4529, testing earnings resilience in AI and consumer names.
Overnight reverse repo at 0.275 trillion is near zero; a further decline would mechanically lift the liquidity dimension through the 96.47 score produced by the neutral direction rule.

bull_case.title: Bull case: memory de-rating stays contained while credit and volatility remain low
points: No credit contagion: HY OAS at 3.11 percent and IG OAS at 0.83 percent leave the high-yield spread at the neutral 57.91 percentile.
Volatility stays low: VIX at 15.21 sits in the 25.00 percentile with realized volatility at 9.5765, keeping the goldilocks regime intact.
The de-rating narrows: 12 of 22 themes improved versus the prior session, with consumer electronics up 1.8464 percent and digital advertising up 0.8226 percent.
If 2026-10-14 CPI undershoots, the real rate can retreat from 2.91 percent at the 99.68 percentile and the composite can return toward 50.

base_case.title: Base case: caution range-bound with memory the weakest link
points: The composite holds the 50 to 56 band at caution; cross-asset confirmation oscillating near 0.50 makes the score highly sensitive to a few binary signals.
The memory basket (3.3529 percent lower) and semiconductor equipment (2.3011 percent lower) keep dragging AI hardware while other segments recover.
Credit and volatility hold: HY OAS at 3.11 percent and VIX at 15.21; the macro dimension at 73.84 underpins the 53.05 composite.
The trend dimension at 42.49 and price 7.4871 percent above the 200-day average leave the 13.86 percent drawdown from the high in normal-adjustment territory.

bear_case.title: Bear case: a hot CPI plus memory contagion takes the composite back above 57
points: 2026-10-14 CPI comes in hot, the real rate rises further from 2.91 percent in the 99.68 percentile and the 10-year yield moves up from 5.24 percent, lifting the macro dimension above 73.84.
Memory weakness spreads into semiconductor equipment (2.3011 percent lower) and quantum computing (1.7609 percent lower), restarting the AI-hardware de-rating.
Small-cap relative weakness at 9.5212 (negative) and the new-lows ratio at 0.1218 worsen, and breadth breaks below 0.5419.
Cross-asset confirmation returns to 0.75 or higher and VIX moves clearly up from 15.21, taking the composite back above 57 and toward 60.
